title: onprem-install-flaky-network-workarounds-and-verification
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc collects reproducible workarounds, verification commands, and a concise smoke/acceptance test for recurring "flaky network" and terraform-related install failures seen in on-prem / VPC private deployments. It is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, and teams running upgrade/patch windows.

Context summary:
- Problem class: intermittent failures during bootstrap or post-upgrade runtime: node join timeouts, kubelet image pull stalls, terraform apply blocking on routes/security groups, healthchecks flapping between Ready/NotReady.
- Environment: air-gapped or semi-restricted VPCs, customer-provided NAT/proxy, internal private registries, private KMS.

Quick verification checklist (run before / after any change) — 10 minute triage:
1) Network basics (1-2 mins):
   - ping default gateway from host, traceroute to registry/gateway.
   - check DNS: dig +short model-registry.example.local and curl http://<registry-ip>:5000/v2/_catalog | head
   - verify NTP: timedatectl status (offset < 200ms).
2) Terraform sanity (2-3 mins):
   - terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars -refresh -out=plan.tfout (expect no drifting resources blocking apply)
   - terraform state list | tail -n 10 (look for partially created resources like aws_eip or azurerm_network_interface)
   - If state locking fails, check backend lock table / consul: consul kv get terraform/locks/<workspace>
3) K8s / node checks (2 mins):
   - kubectl get nodes -o wide; kubectl describe node <node> for NotReady reasons
   - journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | grep -Ei "image pull|failed|evict"
4) Service / readiness check (2 mins):
   - curl -sSf http://<svc-ip>:8000/healthz and /readiness. Expect 200 within 2s.
   - run small inference curl: POST /v1/generate with a 10 token prompt; ensure response < 1.2s (local cluster) or report latency baseline.

Common failure patterns and pragmatic workarounds:
A) Intermittent DNS resolution in private networks
   Symptom: containers fail to pull images intermittently; repeated "no such host" or timeouts only from kubelet but host DNS okay.
   Root causes we’ve seen: split-horizon DNS misconfig for nodes, ephemeral DNS cache overflow, unresponsive internal resolver.
   Workarounds:
     - Configure /etc/systemd/resolved stub listener off and point /etc/resolv.conf to a stable internal resolver.
     - Add a short-lived cron to rotate systemd-resolved caches during upgrades: systemd-resolve --flush-caches (schedule during maintenance).
     - As last resort, populate critical registry A records in /etc/hosts on nodes (temporary, documented change).

B) Terraform apply blocks on security group / route creation
   Symptom: terraform hangs at "Creating network route" or reports 409 conflicts when re-applying after partial failures.
   Root causes: eventual consistency in cloud vendor API / race between modules.
   Workarounds: 
     - Use terraform apply -parallelism=1 for the module containing network resources to reduce API races.
     - Insert a short null_resource local-exec with sleep 15 between resource groups (ugly but effective) — note in changelog.
     - If using remote state with DynamoDB/consul, verify locks removed: aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"<workspace>"}}'

C) Kubelet stuck on image pull / registry auth failure
   Symptom: pods in ImagePullBackOff only on some nodes; docker login success on nodes when tested.
   Workarounds:
     - Check container runtime creds: cat /etc/docker/config.json (or /etc/containerd/certs.d) for correct auths.
     - Restart node container runtime after clearing overlay: systemctl restart containerd && rm -rf /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.*/* (only if low risk).
     - For flaky proxy auth: set NO_PROXY for internal registries in kubelet.service environment.

D) Healthchecks flip after upgrade due to config drift
   Symptom: services become Ready but return 500s intermittently post-migration.
   Action: check configmap differences: kubectl get configmap -o yaml | diff -u old-config.yaml -
   Workaround: maintain a canonical configmap in TF as part of the deployment (less manual drift).

Terraform module notes (practical, non-ideal patches we've used):
- variable "private_subnet_ids": accept both string and list by normalizing in module with join and split in examples. Documented in module README with sample JSON varfile.
- network module: include optional argument `creation_order = "sequential"` that maps to -parallelism=1 on apply via README guidance.
- S3/backend: enable state locking TTL to 10m for noisy CI environments.
- Provide a lightweight make task: make tf-plan TARGET=network VARS=secrets.tfvars which runs plan and saves plan file with timestamped name for audit.

Upgrade / rollback checklist (recommended short window):
1) Pre-upgrade: run smoke checklist (above), snapshot terraform state, snapshot critical PVs if available.
2) Canary: roll one node/pool with maxUnavailable=1 and run synthetic inference load on it for 5-10 minutes.
3) Roll: proceed with batch rolling updates, watch for pattern regressions. If >3% error rate increase or sustained CPU/IO > 85% on model nodes, pause.
4) Rollback: revert terraform module version in tfvars, terraform apply --target=module.runtime -auto-approve. Rollback note: attach plan outputs and timestamp of last working plan for audit.

Runbook snippets (commands to copy):
- Quick node kubelet logs: journalctl -u kubelet -n 300 --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'
- Show pods in failed states: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide
- Check terraform remote lock (consul): consul kv get -recurse terraform/locks || echo "no locks"
- Simple curl smoke (local cluster): curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":10}' | jq '.choices[0].text'

Acceptance criteria for a healthy install (target):
- All nodes Ready for 5 consecutive minutes.
- All model-serving pods have restart count = 0 and pass /readiness 5/5 times at 10s cadence.
- Terraform plan after apply reports 0 changes (idempotent).
- End-to-end synthetic inference matches baseline latency within 20% and success rate >= 99%.

Notes / follow-ups:
- We should add a small TF module test harness that runs plan+apply in a disposable VPC with -parallelism=1 to detect API races earlier.
- Add a verified host-level playbook for DNS priming on first-boot images.

Appendix: useful logs to attach when escalating:
- /var/log/syslog or journalctl export from node (last 2k lines).
- terraform plan output and state list.
- kubelet logs and kube-apiserver audit snippets.

If you run into a new flaky pattern, drop a short summary in the Jira INF-4821 and tag eng-private-deployments so we can add a reproducible case here.
